title: Eden narrative
summary: Genesis situates the first human pair in a divinely planted garden associated with four rivers. The atlas leaves Eden unpinned because a recoverable modern location is not established.
historicalNote: Map treatment is intentionally literary/geographic rather than a claim to archaeological localization.

title: Ark rests in the mountains of Ararat
summary: Genesis describes the ark resting in the “mountains of Ararat.”
historicalNote: This phrase should not be collapsed into the modern peak called Mount Ararat.

title: Babel and the tower
summary: The Babel narrative is set in Shinar and explains linguistic dispersion in theological/literary terms.
historicalNote: The archaeological city of Babylon is locatable; the narrative’s event-historicity is a separate interpretive question.

title: Abram leaves Haran for Canaan
summary: Genesis describes Abram departing Haran and traveling into Canaan.
historicalNote: The sequence of named locations is textual; the exact route line is reconstructed.

title: Abram goes down to Egypt
summary: A famine prompts Abram to travel from Canaan toward Egypt and later return.

title: Abram and Melchizedek
summary: After the kings narrative, Melchizedek king of Salem blesses Abram.
historicalNote: Salem is mapped at Jerusalem as a probable identification, not an explicit equation within Genesis itself.

title: Sodom and Gomorrah narrative
summary: Genesis 18–19 describes judgment on Sodom and Gomorrah and Lot’s escape toward Zoar.
historicalNote: No definitive archaeological pin is displayed for Sodom or Gomorrah.

title: Binding of Isaac / Akedah
summary: Genesis 22 narrates Abraham traveling to the land of Moriah with Isaac.
historicalNote: The route is reconstructed; the Jerusalem/Temple Mount location is the later canonical/traditional identification, not an archaeologically demonstrated Genesis-era waypoint.

title: Jacob’s dream at Bethel
summary: On the way from Beersheba toward Haran, Jacob names the place Bethel after his dream.

title: Jacob wrestles near the Jabbok
summary: Jacob crosses the Jabbok and receives the name Israel in the Peniel narrative.
historicalNote: The river identification is secure; the exact Peniel site is not.

title: Joseph sold near Dothan
summary: Joseph’s brothers encounter him near Dothan; merchants carry him toward Egypt.
historicalNote: The route line toward Egypt is a corridor reconstruction, not a documented caravan track for this event.

title: Jacob’s household moves to Egypt
summary: After stopping at Beersheba, Jacob’s household travels to Egypt and is settled in Goshen.
historicalNote: Goshen is shown as a broad eastern-Delta anchor rather than a fixed polygon.
